Four actors portray Charbel across his life, with Jerry Ghazal as the younger Charbel and the story's central figure. The film is listed with Lebanese cinemas for 2026. This is a new production, distinct from the 2009 film "Charbel" by Nabil Lebbos.

news.main-charbel-premiere-release-2026-: Charbel Premieres in Beirut; Lebanese Cinema Release Set for October 22

Charbel, the new feature film about Saint Charbel, held its special premiere on October 9 at BlackBox in Beirut Media Zone, according to Nidaa al-Watan's October 10 report. The film is a joint NMPRO and MTV production, directed by Nadim Mehanna and written by Claudia Marshalian, with Jerry Ghazal playing the young Charbel and Father Roukoz El Hajj portraying him later in life. Cinemacity lists a runtime of 130 minutes.

Lebtalks reported that the October 9 launch was under President Joseph Aoun's patronage and would be broadcast on MTV, with a nationwide Lebanese theatrical rollout planned from October 22. Cinemacity Beirut independently lists Thursday, October 22 as its opening date. Its page still has no screening sessions scheduled. The completed premiere and the upcoming public cinema opening are different milestones.

A separate charity screening in support of Anta Akhi is scheduled for October 12 at ABC Achrafieh. International release dates, streaming distribution and English-language availability remain unconfirmed.

news.main-gallery-ai-transformation-seri: From the Historic Photograph to a New Saint Charbel Art Series

We have added an AI transformation series to our gallery, bringing the historic photograph of Saint Charbel into conversation with new devotional art. The original stays visible beside the renditions, so visitors can see the source and the artistic choices for themselves.
The historic reference photograph, not an AI rendition. Photographer unknown; public domain according to Wikimedia Commons.

The collection shows the work as a series, from imagined portraits to close portraits and a comparison strip. The current first candidate has a dark beard with a grey center streak; the window portrait also has a dark beard. Other takes remain visible, so visitors can compare different artistic choices rather than seeing one image presented as a definitive likeness. The final and alternate renditions use the historic photograph as their reference; the early candidates are imagined portraits, not verified transformations of that source photograph.

We are proud to share the series, and we want its meaning to be clear. These are AI-assisted artistic renditions, not newly discovered photographs, a reconstruction of a documented scene or proof of an apparition. The gallery labels the new images as artistic renditions or "AI transformation, not a photograph." The historic photograph remains separately identified and credited. A personal-experience caption on the first candidate is presented as the website creator's own account, not independent verification.

news.main-religious-trails-minister-visi: Lebanese and Jordanian Ministers Visit Saint Charbel's Pilgrimage Sites
Qozhaya monastery, archival venue context, not the ministers' visit. Photo: Yellaban, public domain.

Lebanon's Tourism Minister Laura Al-Khazen Lahoud and Jordan's Tourism and Antiquities Minister Imad Hijazin visited Qozhaya monastery, Bqaa Kafra, Annaya and Saint Charbel's hermitage on Friday, according to the National News Agency's October 3 report. They met priests and monks and were briefed on Lebanon's religious trails, including the Lebanon Mountain Trail and the trail associated with Saint Charbel. The report describes a visit and briefing, not a new agreement or a trail opening.

news.main-kfifan-patron-relics-2026-10-s: Saint Charbel's Formation Monastery Receives Relics from Rome
news.main-kfifan-patron-relics-2026-10-k: Kfifan monastery, 2012. Venue context, not the relic reception. Photo: Evilscaught, CC BY 3.0; WebP conversion.

Kfifan's Monastery of Saints Cyprian and Justina received relics of its two patron saints from Rome, MTV Lebanon reported on October 2. Mass, a blessing and a procession marked their feast. Father Emile Akiki of the Lebanese Maronite Order led the Mass. Saint Charbel studied at Kfifan before his ordination, under Saint Nimatullah Al-Hardini. The report also recalls the monastery's connection with Blessed Estephan Nehme. These are relics of Cyprian and Justina, not Saint Charbel. The ceremony's exact calendar date is not specified.

news.main-douaihy-hoayek-altar-consecrat: September 27, 2026 · Altar consecration in Beirut · Reported October 6
Beirut Cathedral Consecrates an Altar to Blessed Patriarchs Douaihy and Hoayek
Saint George Maronite Cathedral (left) and the Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque, downtown Beirut, 2009. Venue context, not the consecration Mass. Photo: Lebnen18, CC BY-SA 3.0; WebP conversion.

On Sunday, September 27, Maronite Patriarch Cardinal Bechara Boutros Al-Rahi presided over the consecration of an altar dedicated to Blessed Patriarchs Estephan Douaihy and Elias Hoayek at Saint George Maronite Cathedral in downtown Beirut, with the two patriarchs' relics placed within it. President Joseph Aoun attended, alongside religious and official figures and faithful from across Lebanon, especially Zgharta-Ehden, Douaihy's birthplace region. In his homily, Al-Rahi paired the two blesseds: Douaihy "preserved the church's memory and heritage amidst persecution," while Hoayek "carried the nation's cause amidst major transformations." Both remain Blessed, not canonized saints: Douaihy was beatified in 2024, Hoayek on July 25, 2026.

news.main-emmitsburg-shrine-anniversary-: Emmitsburg Celebrates Nine Years of Saint Sharbel's Shrine
National Shrine Grotto, Emmitsburg, 2015. Venue context, not the 2026 celebration. Photo: Bohemian Baltimore, CC BY-SA 4.0; resized to WebP.

The Family of Saint Sharbel USA reports that pilgrims gathered on September 26 at the National Shrine Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes in Emmitsburg, Maryland, for the ninth anniversary of Saint Sharbel's shrine dedication. The celebration included Eucharistic Adoration, confessions and Mass celebrated by Father Theodore Trinko, IVE, at St. Mary's Glass Chapel. After Mass, pilgrims followed the saint's relic in procession to the shrine, where they received a blessing with Saint Sharbel's oil and venerated the relic. The organizer published its account on September 30.

news.main-byblos-annaya-prayer-walk-2026: Prayer Walk from Byblos to Annaya for South Lebanon's Christians
At the monastery entrance in Annaya, where the walk ends: a pilgrim reaches up to Saint Charbel's statue. Photograph: LLEW,

On September 26, pilgrims walked from Byblos to Annaya carrying the intentions of the Christians who remain in Lebanon's southern border villages - Rmeich, Ain Ebel, Debel - turning the journey into an act of solidarity and hope. Believers from across Lebanon gathered in Byblos and walked some 10 miles from the Mar Girgis church to the Monastery of Saint Maron in Annaya, where the pilgrimage concluded with Mass at the Church of Saint Charbel. Organizer Anthony Jarjour of Rmeich, who walked some 112 miles from Rmeich to Annaya last year, had set out from Tyre on September 22 and reached the shrine after five days on foot - about 93 miles, rerouted for road closures. The pilgrimage was organized with the Monastery of St. Maron in Annaya and the municipalities of Byblos and Annaya, with Civil Defense and Red Cross support.

news.main-hoayek-beatification-2026-07-m: Maronite Patriarch Elias Hoayek Beatified at Dimane
news.main-hoayek-beatification-2026-07-o: On Saturday, July 25, 2026, Elias Hoayek, Maronite Patriarch of Antioch from 1899 to 1931, was beatified at the Patriarchal summer seat of Dimane in Lebanon. Vatican News reports that President Joseph Aoun attended, that Cardinal Marcello Semeraro, prefect of the Dicastery for the Causes of Saints, concelebrated as the envoy of Pope Leo XIV, and that Patriarch Bechara Boutros al-Rai gave the homily. From that day he is called Blessed. The miracle for his beatification was approved by decree on May 22, 2026. At the Angelus the next day, Pope Leo XIV called him "a man of dialogue and hope" and the "Father of Greater Lebanon." news.main-monte-sole-beatification-2026-: Three Priests Martyred at Monte Sole Beatified in Bologna
Inside the sacrario, the memorial to the fallen at Marzabotto on the Monte Sole ridge, where the 1944 massacres took place. Photograph: Gianni Careddu,

On Sunday, September 27, in the Basilica of San Petronio in Bologna, Cardinal Marcello Semeraro, prefect of the Dicastery for the Causes of Saints, beatified three priests killed by Nazi forces in the 1944 Monte Sole massacres: Don Ubaldo Marchioni, a diocesan priest; Don Elia Comini, a Salesian; and Father Martino Capelli, a Dehonian. Because the Church has recognized them as martyrs, no miracle was required for their beatification - from Sunday they are called Blessed. Bologna Today reported that a bullet-pierced pyx, found in the rubble of the altar of Casaglia's church, has become a symbol of the massacre the three priests did not escape.
news.main-fulton-sheen-beatification-202: Fulton Sheen Beatified in Saint Louis Before 50,000
Blessed Fulton Sheen at his desk in 1956, at the height of his television years.
Archbishop Fulton J. Sheen - the Emmy-winning broadcaster of

- was declared Blessed at a Mass in The Dome at America's Center in Saint Louis, Missouri. Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle presided for Pope Leo XIV before a crowd organizers estimated near 50,000; the miracle that cleared the way was the 2010 revival of James Fulton Engstrom, who carried Sheen's relic in the procession. A day earlier, Pope Leo XIV praised Sheen's media apostolate at the Wednesday General Audience. He is Blessed, not yet a saint - his cause for canonization continues.
